title: Wine Wimsey Review · Wed Nov 25
subtitle: NEW-VOICE test batch 3. Replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 25 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder. 8 character feed posts + 2 stories. All posts use the locked cartoon character with a rotating expression and an action. Captions and first comments included. No TOBIs, no plain cards. Seasonal: #06 (Thanksgiving leftovers, night before). Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and 2 stories and said upload on Nov 24. First-comment delays randomized (1-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: The cereal was $6.99. / Or $3.49 if I download the app, make an account, and let them track me forever. / Just charge me the real price.
posts.caption: Same box, same aisle, same Tuesday. One price for people who hand over their email, birthday and shopping habits, and a 'regular' price for the rest of us that's somehow double.
posts.first: I paid the $6.99 out of pure spite. The cashier looked at me like I'd lost my mind.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses in a grocery aisle, a blue glow around her. She smirks with one eyebrow raised and taps a yellow shelf tag that says $6.99 and $3.49 WITH APP, a bottle of wine in her shopping cart. Text at the top reads: The cereal was $6.99. Or $3.49 if I download the app, make an account, and let them track me forever. A pink box at the bottom reads: Just charge me the real price.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: one raised eyebrow smirk, tapping the shelf price tag

posts.quote: When I was a kid, neighbors borrowed a cup of sugar and stayed for coffee. / Now we only talk through the doorbell camera app. / I miss Doris.
posts.caption: Doris next door knew my kids' names, my car, and when I was sick, and she showed up with soup. Now I get a phone alert that a 'person was detected' and it's the mailman.
posts.first: I know my current neighbors mostly by their dogs. One of them I've only ever seen in a bathrobe.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1984: a smiling woman in a blue shirt hands a cup of sugar to an older neighbor at the door. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses side-eyes a phone showing a doorbell camera view of a house. Text at the top reads: When I was a kid, neighbors borrowed a cup of sugar and stayed for coffee. Now we only talk through the doorbell camera app. A teal box at the bottom reads: I miss Doris.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: young-her smiling handing over a cup of sugar; now: skeptical sideways eye-roll at the doorbell camera on her phone

posts.quote: If you're 15 minutes late, a text is free. / Don't walk in saying 'traffic was crazy.' / Traffic is always crazy. Leave earlier.
posts.caption: Everybody has a phone in their hand every waking minute of the day. 'Running 15 behind' is three words. It takes less time than the excuse you're rehearsing in the parking lot.
posts.first: I'm the one who shows up ten minutes early and sits in the car. My mother raised me that way and I can't shake it.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on a teal dotted background. She looks unimpressed with heavy-lidded eyes and taps a wristwatch on her raised left wrist. Text at the top reads: If you're 15 minutes late, a text is free. Don't walk in saying 'traffic was crazy.' A red box at the bottom reads: Traffic is always crazy. Leave earlier.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: unimpressed heavy-lidded look, tapping her wristwatch

posts.quote: My printer stopped working because the ink 'wasn't genuine.' / It's ink. / I didn't ask for its family tree.
posts.caption: The cartridge was half the price, it fit perfectly, and it was black. Just black. The printer took one look at it and decided it would rather not print my one page.
posts.first: I ended up driving to the library to print it. Ten cents a page and nobody questioned my ink.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a desk, an orange glow around her. She pulls her glasses down her nose, side-eyes a printer, and points at a screen that says INK NOT RECOGNIZED, with blank paper on the desk. Text at the top reads: My printer stopped working because the ink 'wasn't genuine.' It's ink. An orange box at the bottom reads: I didn't ask for its family tree.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: side-eye over glasses pulled down her nose, pointing at the printer's INK NOT RECOGNIZED screen

posts.quote: In 1982 a washer lasted twenty years. / Mine is four, needs a $300 circuit board, and plays a song when it's done. / Nobody asked for the song.
posts.caption: My mother's washer moved with us twice and was still running when she sold the house. Mine has Wi-Fi, a touch screen, and an error code I had to look up on YouTube.
posts.first: The repairman said they just don't make them like they used to. He said it like I didn't already know.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1982: a smiling woman loads colorful laundry into a green top-loading washer. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses grimaces with gritted teeth, holding a $300 estimate, musical notes floating from a modern front-load washer. Text at the top reads: In 1982 a washer lasted twenty years. Mine is four, needs a $300 circuit board, and plays a song when it's done. A purple box at the bottom reads: Nobody asked for the song.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: twitchy gritted-teeth grimace, holding the $300 repair estimate like evidence

posts.quote: If you're coming to Thanksgiving empty-handed, / you don't get to bring empty containers for leftovers. / That's not how this works, Gary.
posts.caption: Bring a pie. Bring rolls. Bring a bag of ice from the gas station, I don't care. But don't walk in with nothing and leave with a week of turkey in my good containers.
posts.first: I've lost more Tupperware at holidays than I've ever lost socks. I'm starting to write my name on the lids.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on an orange dotted background. She smirks smugly and holds up an open empty plastic leftovers container, pointing at it. Text at the top reads: If you're coming to Thanksgiving empty-handed, you don't get to bring empty containers for leftovers. A teal box at the bottom reads: That's not how this works, Gary.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24; seasonal (Thanksgiving leftovers, night before)
posts.expression: smug satisfied smirk, holding up an empty leftovers container

posts.quote: Call me crazy, but if you park across two spaces so your car doesn't get a ding, / you already have a dent. / It's in your manners.
posts.caption: Half the lot was empty and he still parked crooked across the two closest spots to the door. The rest of us walked a little farther so his car could feel special.
posts.first: I parked right next to him anyway. Close, but legal.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses in a parking lot, a lime glow around her, one hand on her hip, pointing at a lime-green sports car parked across two spaces. Her mouth is open in an 'are you kidding me' squint. Text at the top reads: Call me crazy, but if you park across two spaces so your car doesn't get a ding, A red box at the bottom reads: You already have a dent. It's in your manners.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: open-mouth 'are you kidding me' squint, hand on hip, pointing at the car across two spaces

posts.quote: My phone plan is $40 a month. / The bill says $63.17. / It's an 'administrative fee.' / I'm the one doing all the administering.
posts.caption: Then there's a 'recovery charge,' an 'access fee,' and a line that just says 'other.' Other. I'm paying $23 a month for 'other' and nobody at the store can tell me what it is.
posts.first: I spent forty minutes on the phone about it. They gave me a $5 credit and a survey.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on a pink dotted background. She grins tightly with a stress vein on her forehead and taps a large phone or tablet that says $63.17. Text at the top reads: My phone plan is $40 a month. The bill says $63.17. It's an 'administrative fee.' A purple box at the bottom reads: I'm the one doing all the administering.
posts.note: new-voice batch 3, approved via upload Nov 24
posts.expression: tight fake 'everything is fine' toothy grin with a stress vein, tapping the $63.17 on her phone
